subject: Post-call: Clarify exactly what is stored for prompts & outputs
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Anna Murphy <anna.murphy@clinify.com>, Samir Desai <samir@clinify.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — quick clarifications on PII storage for prompts & outputs

Thanks for the productive call earlier. Quick recap and a few targeted asks so we can finalize the security section in the proposal. I want to make sure the language we send to your security/compliance team is exact — please confirm the three items below or correct as needed: 

1) What we store from an interaction: we currently described it as "input prompt (sanitized) + generated output (persisted) + ephemeral request/response traces." Does Clinify require full raw prompts (including free-text PII) to be retained, or will redaction/sanitization suffice for your workflow?

2) Retention TTL: our hosted default for persisted outputs is 30 days unless a customer requests a longer retention. Is Clinify asking for a firm retention period (e.g., 90/365 days) or an option to set per-environment TTLs?

3) Logging & access controls: we capture telemetry (timestamps, model/version, token counts) for billing and performance. For anything labeled PII, we can send logs to your VPC only or redact fields and keep aggregated metrics in the hosted console — which approach does your security team prefer?

Attachments: I attached a short summary of the retention options and a spreadsheet for you to mark required retention periods by data class.

Next steps I propose: you confirm the three bullets above and mark the spreadsheet; we’ll then produce a short paragraph you can include in your SOC/Procurement packet.

Thanks — Soojin
--
Soojin Lee
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

From: Anna Murphy <anna.murphy@clinify.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Desai <samir@clinify.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — quick clarifications on PII storage for prompts & outputs

Thanks Soojin — great summary. A couple clarifications from our side before we mark the spreadsheet: 

- For (1): We need the raw prompt for a small percentage of audit-trail use cases (clinical dispute investigation). Ideally we want a configurable flag per-environment: "persist_raw_prompts: true/false". If set to true, raw prompts must be stored encrypted and access audited.

- For (2): Default retention should be 30 days, but for audit-enabled environments we need up to 365 days. We prefer TTLs be configurable per-environment and per-data-class (raw_prompt, sanitized_prompt, output, telemetry).

- For (3): We want logs with PII stripped to remain in hosted console for analytics. Full, unredacted logs should be routed to our VPC bucket and retained under our controls. Also: can you confirm whether stored outputs are encrypted with customer-provided keys (KMS) when routed to VPC?

One more ask: does Redwood persist intermediate KV cache entries (e.g., rolling session state) beyond the immediate request? If yes, what's the retention and is that exposed to us as a data class?

I'll update the spreadsheet today.

—Anna
Anna Murphy
Head of Product, Clinify Health
anna.murphy@clinify.com | +1 415 555 0199
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Anna Murphy <anna.murphy@clinify.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T20:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — quick clarifications on PII storage for prompts & outputs

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear asks, I’m on the infra/arch side and can confirm how our platform handles each item today and options we can offer: 

1) Raw prompts: We support a per-environment toggle "persist_raw_prompts". If enabled, we persist the raw prompt to the customer VPC object store (S3-compatible) only. When persisted to your VPC we encrypt at rest with your KMS key (we do not hold the key). For hosted-only customers who do not route logs to a VPC, raw prompts can be persisted encrypted with Redwood-managed keys but we can also offer automatic redaction before storage.

2) TTLs: By default we set output retention to 30 days for hosted routing. We support environment-level TTLs up to 365 days for outputs and up to 730 days for raw prompts when required for audits. The TTL is configurable per-data-class (raw_prompt, sanitized_prompt, output, kv_cache, telemetry).

3) Logging & access routing: PII-stripped telemetry is kept in the hosted console (aggregated metrics + anonymized traces). Full unredacted logs/output/requests are supportably delivered to your VPC bucket via server-side transfer; once in the VPC they are under your lifecycle rules. Access to persisted PII in-hosted contexts is restricted to RBAC roles in Redwood and we can provide audit logs for any access events.

4) KV cache: KV cache entries (in-memory fast cache for model context) are ephemeral by default and are not persisted to disk in the hosted offering. If you enable session snapshotting for long-running conversations we persist snapshots to your VPC only and those snapshots follow the TTL you configure (snapshot_ttl).

Attachments: see the enclosed short tech note (redwood-prompt-retention-outline.pdf) that maps data classes to default settings and the configuration flags you can toggle.

If you want, we can produce an appendix paragraph for your procurement packet that states the exact wording we recommend (KMS usage, TTL ranges, routing options).

Thanks — Aditya
Aditya Rao
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-22T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — quick clarifications on PII storage for prompts & outputs

Anna — thanks for the spreadsheet. Per the answers above, here are the concrete next steps to finish the security section: 

- Clinify to mark per-environment flags in the spreadsheet (persist_raw_prompts: true/false, snapshot_ttl, output_ttl).
- Redwood to provide a short "storage & retention" paragraph with exact wording, plus an optional DocuSign acceptance field for the retention appendix (we’ll add DocuSign link).
- If persist_raw_prompts is true: Redwood will configure outbound routing to Clinify’s VPC and configure KMS key policy so Clinify retains key control. We’ll provide the task list for your infra team.

I attached the spreadsheet back with our suggested defaults filled. If that looks good we’ll add the paragraph to the proposal and send the DocuSign link for the appendix.

Best — Monica
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
